title: Talent scouting sprint and asymmetric interview rubric
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a compact playbook for a 10-workday talent-scouting sprint focused on mid‑level IC and contractor-to-perm pipelines. It pairs a short outward sourcing blitz with an "asymmetric" interview rubric designed to reveal signal quickly while minimizing candidate fatigue. Use this when we need fast, high‑precision slates for roles where practical problem solving and cross-team collaboration matter (platform, infra, applied ML).

Scope / When to use:
- Fast replacement hiring (2–4 week time-to-offer target)
- Contract-to-perm trials after a short paid engagement
- High-volume follow-up slates from campus or event sourcing

Sprint overview (10 workdays):
Phase A — Sourcing & Pre-qualification (Days 1–3)
- Day 1: Kickoff with hiring manager and hiring panel: 30m alignment on must-have skills, risk signals, and non-negotiables.
- Day 1–2: Rapid sourcing blitz (LinkedIn InMails, referrals, event follow-ups). Each sourcer targets 12 prospects.
- Day 3: Phone screen batch (30m) with a checklist: role fit, 2 technical probes, 1 culture question. Mark as green/yellow/red.

Phase B — Asymmetric interviews (Days 4–7)
- Concept: asymmetric = different short-form probes per interviewer tailored to reveal orthogonal signals rather than repeating the same whiteboard problem. Less redundancy, more breadth.
- Interview structure (60m total):
  * 10m intro / expectations / logistics (interviewer rotates)
  * 25m practical probe (candidate picks 1 of 2 tracks: systems-design-lite OR live-debug/code-review)
  * 15m collaboration exercise (design conversation with a buddy from a cross-functional team)
  * 10m wrap + candidate questions
- Interviewer assignments: one technical lead (deep), one systems collaborator (broad), one people-collab/values interviewer. Rotate across panel to reduce bias.

Phase C — Decision & Short trial offer (Days 8–10)
- Day 8: Calibration meeting — reviewers present quick evidence packets (one paragraph per interviewer: strengths, risk, recommended next step). Use 1–5 numeric score per axis.
- Day 9: Optionally extend 1–2 week paid trial offer for borderline/high-potential candidates (trial brief attached to offer).
- Day 10: Finalize offer or feedback.

Asymmetric interview rubric (compact, for fast calibration):
Scoring axes (each 1–5):
- Core competency: role-specific technical ability to perform day‑1 tasks.
- Problem decomposition: clarity in breaking ambiguous problems into steps.
- Production judgment: tradeoffs, cost/latency/security considerations.
- Collaboration signal: communication with cross‑functional partners.
- Learning velocity: evidence of picking up new domains quickly.
- Hire-risk modifiers (qualitative): attention to detail, response to failure, cultural fit concerns.

Scoring guidance: 
- 5 = immediate unblocker; could mentor juniors on this area. Clear examples + past impact.
- 3 = competent but needs ramp; typical mid-level profile.
- 1 = misses multiple must-haves or demonstrates key risk.

Normalization heuristics for calibration (quick):
- Drop one highest and one lowest numeric score from panel if >2 interviewers, then average.
- If disagreement >2 points between reviewers on Core competency, require a fast second-look technical take (15–30m).
- For contractors considered for perm, weight Trial performance x1.4 in final decision.

Sample practical probes (pick 1 of 2 per candidate):
- Systems design-lite: "Design a lightweight inference routing layer that can route requests by latency constraint and model cost. Sketch API surfaces and two key failure modes." (expect a 25m scoped answer with tradeoffs).
- Live debug/code-review: "Here's a 15–30 line pseudo-service that leaks memory under load. Walk us through detection and a short remediation plan."

Collaboration exercise prompts (15m):
- "You just joined a week ago. The product team says API latency doubled after last deploy. How do you approach the investigation and what immediate mitigations do you propose?"
- Allow interviewers to role-play product support questions; judge judgement and communication.

Candidate experience & fairness notes:
- Communicate timeline up front: 10 workdays from first contact to decision.
- Offer at least one scheduling window outside core hours for timezone coverage.
- Explain trial offer terms transparently (pay, expected deliverables, evaluation criteria).
- Ensure at least one interviewer has taken bias training in past 12 months.

Onboarding quick-convert checklist (for contract-to-perm or fast hires):
- Pre-onboard: manager writes 3 impact goals for first 30 days and 60 days.
- Day 0: Welcome packet + 60m buddy intro meeting (buddy is from cross-team and will schedule 3 short check-ins in week 1).
- Week 1: First deliverable: small ticket with production-readme + unit tests.
- Week 2–4: Mentor checkpoints: 30m twice weekly first two weeks, then weekly.
- 30-day calibration: hiring manager + mentor + people ops discuss signals for perm conversion.

Mentor-pair micro-rituals (to speed role fit):
- 10–15m daily async update in Slack channel (#onboard-<name>) for first 10 days.
- Twice-weekly 1:1 pairing session focused on codebase walkthroughs — pre-added agenda.
- End-of-week written note from mentor with 3 progress bullets and 1 recommended next focus.

Operational templates (copy/paste snippets):
- Quick evidence packet template: 1) candidate name + role, 2) 2–3 sentence strengths, 3) 2–3 sentence risks, 4) numeric scores per axis, 5) recommended next step.
- Trial brief (one-paragraph): objective, deliverable, evaluator, compensation, time window.

Implementation notes & questions for hiring manager:
- Is a trial part of the org's budget for this role? (pre-approve budget lines).
- Which two signals are non-negotiable? (list them so sourcers can close faster).
- Who will be the onboarding buddy if we convert?

Next steps & ownership:
- People Ops (owner: Maya Chen): spin this into a canned hiring kit + calendar templates.
- Hiring manager: fill must-have list and provide 3 sample tickets suitable for a 1–2 week trial.
- Sourcing team: run Day 1 blitz and deliver initial 12 prospects per sourcer.

Appendix (quick):
- Typical timings: phone screen 30m, asymmetric panel 60m, calibration 30m.
- Fairness checklist: at least one structured question per axis, record notes in rubric template, avoid surprise technical tests outside scheduled time.

Feedback log (workspace): please leave comments inline in this doc with improvements and edge cases.
